revenue_segments.name: Entertainment
revenue_segments.revenue: 11,345 USD millions (Q3 FY26); segment operating income 1,680
revenue_segments.commentary: Subscription and affiliate fees were 7,545 (+12%: Fubo +4%, rates +3%, subscribers +3%, FX +1%). Advertising was 1,625 (-1%, rates -4%). Content sales were 1,596 (-6%). Operating income benefited from lower marketing costs and lower film impairments. A+E impairment of $812M is excluded from segment operating income.
revenue_segments.source_citation: 10-Q Item 2 MD&A, Business Segment Results – Entertainment; Note 2

revenue_segments.name: Sports
revenue_segments.revenue: 4,500 USD millions (Q3 FY26); segment operating income 858
revenue_segments.commentary: Subscription and affiliate fees were 3,142 (+8%: rates +5%, NFL Transaction +4%). Advertising was 1,204 (+5%). Other revenue fell 41% on the absence of UFC pay-per-view. forward_guidance.text: Management expects fiscal 2026 spend on produced and licensed content, including sports rights, of about $24B (vs $23B in fiscal 2025) and capital expenditures of about $9B (vs $8B), driven by Experiences expansion and new attractions, partly offset by lower cruise fleet spending. The company targets at least $9B of share repurchases in fiscal 2026 ($7.2B done through nine months). The sale of its 50% A+E interest to a Hearst affiliate for ~$1.2B cash is expected to close by the end of fiscal 2026. Much of Consumer Products will move into the Entertainment segment starting with fiscal 2027 reporting. About $2B of contracted performance-obligation revenue is expected in the remainder of fiscal 2026. The 10-Q gives no quantitative revenue, EPS or segment operating income guidance for Q4 or the full year.
forward_guidance.source_citation: 10-Q Item 2 MD&A, Financial Condition (Produced and licensed programming costs, Investing Activities, Financing Activities); Note 17 Subsequent Events; Note 2 Segment Information; Note 3 Revenues

key_risks.description: Carriage and programming contract renewal risk. NFL Network and NFL RedZone were removed from Comcast Xfinity in Q3 FY26 and not reinstated. Disney channels were temporarily dropped from YouTube TV in Q1 FY26. Further renewals for contracts expiring in fiscal 2026 could cause blackouts, and rights costs keep rising.

bull_case: Experiences is accelerating: Q3 revenue +10% and operating income +20% ($3,017M), with domestic Parks & Experiences operating income +27% and hotel occupancy at 91%. Growth is supported by pricing, volume and new cruise ships (Destiny, Adventure).
Entertainment operating income rose 64% to $1,680M, driven by subscription and affiliate fees +12% (more subscribers, higher effective rates) and lower marketing costs.
Capital return is strong: dividend raised to $0.75 per quarter from $0.50, $7.2B of buybacks in nine months against a target of at least $9B, and diluted share count down to 1,743M from 1,805M.
Cost discipline and portfolio pruning: SG&A fell 4% in Q3, corporate expense fell 19%, and the pending ~$1.2B sale of A+E exits an impaired asset.
Contracted visibility: $16B of remaining performance obligations, and the NFL Network/RedZone and Fubo deals broaden ESPN and live TV reach.
bear_case: Sports operating income fell 17% in Q3 (14% over nine months) as programming costs rose 10%, with costs shifted into Q3 by the NBA renewal. Further rights-cost inflation and subscriber losses (-3% over nine months) pressure margins.
Advertising is soft: Entertainment advertising -1% in Q3 (rates -4%), and content sales -6% on TV/VOD and home entertainment declines.
Reported EPS fell 48% to $1.51 on a tough comparison with a $3.3B tax benefit. Restructuring and impairment charges of $900M and amortization cut EPS by $0.55 in Q3.
Operating cash flow fell 8% over nine months to $12.5B while capex rose to about $9B for FY26, and buybacks were partly debt-funded. Borrowings are $46.0B, with $8.6B current.

Legal and regulatory overhang: securities class action trial set for November 2027, antitrust suits over bundling and the Fubo deal, DISH counterclaims, the FCC early license renewal order, and the Comcast NFL Network blackout.
International Parks & Experiences operating income fell 13% in Q3, and Q3 Experiences costs were helped by tariff refunds that may not repeat.

what_to_watch.text: Fiscal Q4 (quarter ended Oct 3, 2026) results: the 10-Q gives no formal Q4 or full-year EPS or segment guidance, so compare against management commentary on the call.
Experiences momentum: whether per capita spending, cruise days and hotel occupancy hold into the fall quarter, and whether domestic attendance growth (+3% in Q3) continues.
Sports profitability: normalization of NBA rights-cost timing, effects of the Xfinity NFL Network blackout, and rates versus subscriber losses.
Entertainment: advertising rates (-4% in Q3), streaming operating trends, and the fiscal 2027 move of Consumer Products into Entertainment reporting.

Capital return and balance sheet: progress toward the at-least-$9B buyback target ($7.2B done through nine months), the A+E sale closing (~$1.2B expected by fiscal year end), and refinancing of current borrowings.

Legal and regulatory: the Oct 27, 2026 final-approval filing in the Biddle/Fendelander settlement, the Unger arbitration ruling, DISH bankruptcy developments, and any FCC response on early license renewals.

hypotheses_explored.question: Is Experiences strength sustainable enough to offset Sports margin pressure?
hypotheses_explored.summary: Experiences added $501M of operating income YoY in Q3 versus a $179M decline in Sports. Experiences growth is volume-led (guests +4%) with pricing support, but includes tariff-refund tailwinds and a fleet expansion that raises depreciation (+15% in segment D&A). Sports decline was partly timing-related (NBA cost shift into Q3).
evidence_quotes: Segment operating income increased $501 million, to $3,017 million from $2,516 million, due to higher revenues at Parks & Experiences and, to a lesser extent, Consumer Products, partially offset by higher costs.
The NBA contract renewal resulted in a shift of costs from the first half of the year to the third quarter.

hypotheses_explored.question: How much of the YoY EPS decline is non-recurring versus operational?
hypotheses_explored.summary: Prior-year EPS of $2.92 included a $1.56 benefit from the Hulu tax reclassification. Excluding that and other items, the comparison is far less negative; Q3 FY26 items were a $0.55 headwind versus a net +$1.31 benefit last year. Underlying operating income rose 21% (segment OI $5,555M vs $4,575M).
evidence_quotes: The net income and EPS decreases reflected the comparison to a non-cash tax benefit recognized upon a change in Hulu's U.S. income tax classification in the prior-year quarter and, to a lesser extent, an impairment of our investment in A+E in the current quarter.
